$comment: SHARED coordinate-conversion vectors for Apple Vision output (Build 2.5 Step 3B).
Apple Vision reports normalized coordinates with the origin at the BOTTOM-LEFT and y
increasing upward. Every consumer in K Scan — the extraction pipeline, the crop
generator, expo-image-manipulator, and the Android half of this module — uses a
TOP-LEFT origin with y increasing downward.
The conversion must happen EXACTLY ONCE, in IOSPersonDetector. Doing it twice, or
doing it again in JavaScript, places every garment region upside down on the body —
and the failure looks like a detector problem rather than an axis problem, which is
why it gets its own vector file rather than an inline assertion.
Both implementations are checked against THIS file:
Coordinates are normalized, so imageWidth/imageHeight never enter the arithmetic.
They are recorded because the cases exist to prove exactly that: a portrait and a

rects.note: The whole image. Must survive the flip unchanged.
High in the frame. In Vision that is a HIGH y; in top-left space it is y=0.
Low in the frame — feet. In Vision that is y=0; in top-left space it is y=0.7.
Symmetric about the middle, so it is the one case a MISSING flip still passes. It is here to be paired with the others, never relied on alone.
Normalized coordinates carry no aspect. A portrait frame converts identically to a square one.
Same arithmetic as the portrait case. If these two ever diverge, an aspect ratio has leaked into the conversion.

A front-camera capture is already mirrored in PIXELS by the time it reaches this module — mirrorSourcePreparation re-encodes the picker's asset. The conversion must therefore NOT touch x. A subject on the left stays on the left.

A mirror selfie routinely cuts off at the thigh, so Vision returns a box running past the frame. The EDGES are clamped and the person is kept — rejecting the box would reject the most common real input.
A zero-area rect is not a person. Both implementations reject it rather than emitting a sliver.

points.note: A nose sits near the TOP of a standing figure: high Vision y, low top-left y.
x is never touched by the conversion.
Vision occasionally reports a joint just outside the frame for an occluded limb.
